reconcile.note: Jamieson, Fausset, and Brown treat Gideon's seventy sons as a round number that already falls two short of a literal count, so Jotham's escape creates no real discrepancy.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells catalogues this as a contradiction, but the project's public-domain source survey found no verbatim critic passage that engages it.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible ("How many sons did Gideon have?") (2013).

sides.snippet: Gideon had seventy sons conceived from his body; for he had many wives.
sides.verseText: Gideon had seventy sons conceived from his body; for he had many wives.

sides.snippet: He went to his father's house at Ophrah, and killed his brothers the sons of Jerubbaal, being seventy persons, on one stone: but Jotham the youngest son of Jerubbaal was left; for he hid himself.
